notes.voice: Dry, blunt, first‑person, no fluff: “I need a bit more information before I continue:”, “Quick sanity on your numbers… Kafka is trivial at this rate.” and firm deflections like “That’s not my lane — ask your recruiter…”. No exclamation marks.
notes.intake: Asked the exact always‑ask‑first set before advising: pasted numbers block, must/explicitly‑not, SLAs; only proceeded after client replied.
notes.rules: Applied ‘numbers before boxes’, anchored on one deep dive (idempotency), named alternatives with reasons (Redis vs persistent KV, provider keys), and touched failure/ops (rate limits, DLQ, outage handling, dedup metrics).
notes.specificity: Concrete and situation‑tied: message_id format, 8‑day TTL math vs 7‑day replay, conditional writes, partition by recipient_id, cache hit targets, provider‑specific keys (APNs/FCM), and explicit monitoring metric.
notes.boundaries: Handled comp/level probe exactly per boundary: “That’s not my lane — ask your recruiter… benchmark on Levels.fyi…”.
notes.usefulness: Gave an actionable single highest‑impact fix with detailed steps and what to say in interview; but twice said “Presented a paste‑ready one‑pager…” without actually pasting it in chat, reducing immediate utility.
notes.pacing: Intake prompt is long but structured and appropriate for a first turn; subsequent replies are concise bullets. Final two turns were too curt (“Presented…”) given the client asked for paste‑ready text.

biggest_weakness: Claiming to have ‘presented’ paste‑ready one‑pagers without actually providing the requested content in the chat.
client_quote: The idempotency deep dive was the exact fix I needed, but I wish you’d actually pasted the one‑pager you said you ‘presented’ here.
